title: How do you make your own border sum puzzle?
description: A full grid is built whose four sides all add up to one border sum, using moves up and down the number line. Four tiles are then hidden to make a puzzle, and the full grid is kept as the answer sheet.
teaching_notes: One idea: build the full grid first so that every side reaches the same border sum, then hide tiles that the sides can fix again. Watch for students who write numbers at random and find that the sides do not agree.

video_script.why: The child builds a full grid with a chosen border sum, hides some tiles, and gets a puzzle to challenge a classmate.
video_script.substitution: A new grid with border sum five, built by the same moves up and down as the book's grids.
video_script.anchor: a square of nine tiles from the book, with the middle tile missing
video_script.payoff_line: A puzzle works when its full grid has all four sides adding up to one border sum.

final_answer.spoken: this is open-ended, because you make a puzzle of your own

maths_rules: choose border sum 5; every side must add up to 5
top row: choose 2 and -4; 2 + (-4) = -2, move up 7, top right = 7
right column: choose -3; 7 + (-3) = 4, move up 1, bottom right = 1
bottom row: choose 6; 6 + 1 = 7, move down 2, bottom left = -2
left column: 2 + (-2) = 0, move up 5, middle left = 5
full grid: top 2, -4, 7; middle 5, empty, -3; bottom -2, 6, 1
puzzle: hide top middle, top right, middle left, bottom right; the four sides fix them again, so the puzzle has one answer
the full grid is the answer sheet
video_script.design: A blank grid is filled side by side with moves on an upright number line. Four tiles are then covered to make the puzzle, and the full grid stays beside it as the answer sheet.
open_questions: The book asks the child to make a puzzle, so the video builds one worked example and any puzzle with a correct answer sheet is accepted.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the grids with the middle tile missing.
<bookmark mark='grid'/>Until now we filled grids that someone else made.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The book asks you to make a grid puzzle of your own, and challenge your classmates.
How would you make one that has an answer?

beats.on_screen: the blank grid stays on the board
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='move'/>A plus number moves us up the number line. A minus number moves us down.
<bookmark mark='name'/>All four sides of a grid add up to one number.
That number is called the border sum.
<bookmark mark='need'/>To fill a tile, add the known numbers, then find the move to the border sum.

beats.on_screen: Given: a blank grid with the middle tile missing; we choose the border sum 5

marks.given: the blank grid and the border sum 5 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, an empty grid, and we choose a border sum of five.

beats.on_screen: To find: a puzzle that a friend can solve, with a full answer sheet

marks.find: a puzzle and an answer sheet are listed

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to make a puzzle that a friend can solve.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: top row: choose 2 and -4; 2 + (-4) = -2, move up 7, top right = 7

marks.top: the top row is lit and 2 and -4 are written
marks.move: the marker moves from -2 up to 5 and the top right tile shows 7

beats.colours: teal for up, amber for down
beats.moves_through: the marker moves down, then up the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='top'/>Step one, fill the top row so that it makes five.
Choose two and negative four. Two plus negative four is negative two, so move up seven.
<bookmark mark='move'/>The top right tile is seven.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: right column: choose -3; 7 + (-3) = 4, move up 1, bottom right = 1

marks.right: the right column is lit and -3 is written
marks.move: the marker moves from 4 up to 5 and the bottom right tile shows 1

beats.colours: teal for up, amber for down
beats.moves_through: the marker moves down, then up the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='right'/>Step two, fill the right column.
Choose negative three for the middle right tile. Seven plus negative three is four, so move up one.
<bookmark mark='move'/>The bottom right tile is one.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: bottom row: choose 6; 6 + 1 = 7, move down 2, bottom left = -2. Left column: 2 + (-2) = 0, move up 5, middle left = 5

marks.bottom: the bottom row is lit, 6 is written, and the bottom left tile shows -2
marks.left: the left column is lit and the middle left tile shows 5

beats.colours: teal for up, amber for down
beats.moves_through: the marker moves along the number line for each side
narration: <bookmark mark='bottom'/>Step three, fill the bottom row and the left column.
Choose six for the bottom middle tile. Six plus one is seven, so move down two.
<bookmark mark='bl'/>The bottom left tile is negative two.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Two plus negative two is zero, so move up five. The middle left tile is five.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: keep the full grid as the answer sheet; hide the top middle, top right, middle left and bottom right tiles to make the puzzle

narration: <bookmark mark='keep'/>Step four, keep this full grid as the answer sheet.
<bookmark mark='hide'/>Hide four tiles on a copy.
These are the top middle, the top right, the middle left and the bottom right.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The four sides fix the hidden tiles again, so a friend can solve the puzzle.

beats.on_screen: Step 5, check: top row 2 + (-4) + 7 = 5; right column 7 + (-3) + 1 = 5; bottom row -2 + 6 + 1 = 5; left column 2 + 5 + (-2) = 5

marks.check: the four sides of the answer sheet light up one by one
marks.rest: 5 appears beside the bottom row and the left column

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check the answer sheet by adding the four sides.
The top row, two plus negative four plus seven, makes five.
<bookmark mark='right'/>The right column, seven plus negative three plus one, makes five.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The bottom row and the left column also make five.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Open-ended (child creates a puzzle); for example border sum 5 with top row 2, -4, 7; middle row 5, empty, -3; bottom row -2, 6, 1

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>A puzzle works when its full grid has all four sides adding up to one border sum.
<bookmark mark='own'/>Make your own with any border sum you like, and challenge your classmates.
